papers.title: Multi-Granularity Cross-Attention Mixture-of-Experts for Protein–Ligand Dissociation Kinetics Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Drug–target affinity prediction is pivotal in drug discovery. However, most existing computational methods focus primarily on binding affinity and do not explicitly model dissociation kinetics ( K off ). Accurately predicting K off therefore remains both important and challenging for kinetics-guided drug screening and residence-time optimization. Results To address this challenge, we propose MGCA, a multi-granularity cross-attention framework for K off prediction. MGCA represents proteins using multi-depth ESM2 features and ligands using multi-radius Morgan fingerprints. It integrates these representations through gated expert fusion, low-rank bidirectional cross-attention, and protein-anchored residual fusion. Across the Zhao dissociation-kinetics dataset and the KinetX benchmark, MGCA achieved the lowest mean squared error (MSE) in all warm-start and protein cold-start evaluations. Notably, MGCA reduced protein cold-start MSE by 42.5% and 12.1% relative to the recent kinetics-specific BiCoA-Net model on Zhao and KinetX, respectively. Under matched hardware, MGCA also trained substantially faster than BiCoA-Net and MoE-Kinetic. Ablation and case-study analyses further showed that MGCA effectively integrates protein, ligand, and interaction information, supporting cross-target generalization, within-target compound ranking, and feature-level interpretation. Together, these results establish MGCA as an accurate, efficient, and interpretable framework for protein–ligand dissociation kinetics prediction. Availability and implementation The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/MGCA-koff and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22932383

papers.primary_summary_zh: 药物靶点亲和力预测在药物发现中至关重要。然而，大多数现有的计算方法主要关注结合亲和力，并没有明确模拟解离动力学（K off）。因此，准确预测 K off 对于动力学引导的药物筛选和停留时间优化既重要又具有挑战性。结果为了应对这一挑战，我们提出了 MGCA，一种用于 K off 预测的多粒度交叉注意力框架。 MGCA 使用多深度 ESM2 特征表示蛋白质，使用多半径摩根指纹表示配体。它通过门控专家融合、低秩双向交叉注意力和蛋白质锚定残差融合来整合这些表示。在赵解离动力学数据集和 KinetX 基准测试中，MGCA 在所有热启动和蛋白质冷启动评估中实现了最低的均方误差 (MSE)。值得注意的是，相对于Zhao和KinetX上最近的动力学特定BiCoA-Net模型，MGCA分别将蛋白质冷启动MSE降低了42.5%和12.1%。在匹配的硬件下，MGCA 的训练速度也明显快于 BiCoA-Net 和 MoE-Kinetic。消融和案例研究分析进一步表明，MGCA 有效地整合了蛋白质、配体和相互作用信息，支持跨目标泛化、目标内化合物排序和特征级解释。总之，这些结果使 MGCA 成为蛋白质-配体解离动力学预测的准确、高效和可解释的框架。可用性和实现源代码和数据集可在 https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/MGCA-koff 和 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22932383 获取

all_papers.title: Multi-Granularity Cross-Attention Mixture-of-Experts for Protein–Ligand Dissociation Kinetics Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Drug–target affinity prediction is pivotal in drug discovery. However, most existing computational methods focus primarily on binding affinity and do not explicitly model dissociation kinetics ( K off ). Accurately predicting K off therefore remains both important and challenging for kinetics-guided drug screening and residence-time optimization. Results To address this challenge, we propose MGCA, a multi-granularity cross-attention framework for K off prediction. MGCA represents proteins using multi-depth ESM2 features and ligands using multi-radius Morgan fingerprints. It integrates these representations through gated expert fusion, low-rank bidirectional cross-attention, and protein-anchored residual fusion. Across the Zhao dissociation-kinetics dataset and the KinetX benchmark, MGCA achieved the lowest mean squared error (MSE) in all warm-start and protein cold-start evaluations. Notably, MGCA reduced protein cold-start MSE by 42.5% and 12.1% relative to the recent kinetics-specific BiCoA-Net model on Zhao and KinetX, respectively. Under matched hardware, MGCA also trained substantially faster than BiCoA-Net and MoE-Kinetic. Ablation and case-study analyses further showed that MGCA effectively integrates protein, ligand, and interaction information, supporting cross-target generalization, within-target compound ranking, and feature-level interpretation. Together, these results establish MGCA as an accurate, efficient, and interpretable framework for protein–ligand dissociation kinetics prediction. Availability and implementation The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/MGCA-koff and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22932383
